instruction.text: Alan was arrested in 1952, for being in a relationship with another man.

atoms.a: Do you think this was right?

feedback.finish: No, this was not right! But unfortunately, being gay was illegal in the UK until 1967.

hint.text: It is important to know that medical treatment can’t take away feelings for people, and you can’t change who you love.
hint.label: Medical treatment

atoms.b: Alan was made to choose between going to ((++prison holiday)) or having medical treatment to take away his feelings for other ((++men women)).
Alan chose to have treatment. However, it didn’t work and he became very ((++depressed happy)).
He then sadly ((++ended started)) his own life in 1954.

instruction.text: Select the image of Queen Elizabeth.

finish.text: Alan Turing received a royal pardon from Queen Elizabeth II in 2013 for his unfair arrest.
finish.sound: Alan Turing received a royal pardon from Queen Elizabuth the second in 2013 for his unfair arrest.

instruction.text: Drag Alan Turing onto the banknote.

feedback.finish: The £50 note now features a picture of Alan. It was released on his birthday in 2021.

atoms.a: Do you think we should be proud of Alan Turing?

feedback.finish: Yes we should! He helped our country during the Second World War and his achievements deserve to be celebrated.
